method.inputs: the WHOLE repo-graph-seed crate. rust/crates/repo-graph-seed/src/pass.rs `build_store`: an entry ENCLOSES (can supply a sentence) only when it carries a non-empty doc AND its stored `subtype` is a canonical TYPE subtype — `ENCLOSING_TYPE_SUBTYPES = ["CLASS", "INTERFACE", "STRUCT", "ENUM"]`, a private const in pass.rs (review SD-F02: RG-REQ-010-L10 says the enclosing TYPE's doc). The set is the type-declaring variants of `indexer::types::NodeSubtype` (types.rs:143-159, serialized SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE) as the extractors emit them: TypeScript class/interface/enum; Java class and record → CLASS (extractor.rs:594-632), interface and `@interface` → INTERFACE (:466-491, :668-688), enum → ENUM; Python class → CLASS; Rust struct → CLASS ('Closest mapping for structs', rust-extractor/src/extractor.rs:482), trait → INTERFACE (:534), enum → ENUM; C/C++ class → CLASS, struct → STRUCT, enum → ENUM. TYPE_ALIAS is excluded (an alias names a type, it declares no member scope; no FRAKTAG METHOD has a documented TYPE_ALIAS name-parent); FUNCTION, VARIABLE, CONSTANT, PROPERTY, METHOD and every other subtype never enclose; the FIRST such entry in corpus order winning (`entry(..).or_insert`) so a duplicated qualified name resolves deterministically (FRAKTAG: 0 duplicated (path, qualified_name) pairs) (`SeedCorpusEntry.qualified_name`/`doc_comment`, ports.rs:61/:67 — no DTO or SQL change: the enclosing type is found by qualified-name containment in the corpus already read); per chunk whose stored `subtype` is exactly `METHOD` (D-SD1-002 as revised by the document review's SD-DEC-01: RG-REQ-010-L10 says 'a method chunk' — properties, constructors, getters, variables and nested types embed exactly as today), `parent_qualified_name(chunk.qualified_name)` and then the LOOKUP RULE (METHOD chunks only; genuine forward declarations — `SeedForwardDecl::ForwardDecl` — are ignored throughout; both steps read the COMPLETE corpus `build_store` receives, before the corpus cap truncates it — only the emitted vectors are cap-limited): the parent qualified name is the chunk's minus its last `.`/`::` segment; (1) if the chunk's own file holds any entry with that qualified name, the enclosing type is decided in that file — the first entry in corpus order with a canonical type subtype (CLASS, INTERFACE, STRUCT, ENUM) and a non-empty doc supplies the sentence, otherwise there is no sentence and the cross-file branch is not consulted; (2) only if the chunk's file holds no such entry, the corpus-wide entries with that qualified name and a canonical type subtype are counted — exactly one, if documented, supplies its sentence; none, or two or more (ambiguous), supply no sentence. Mechanism (review F-SD-001 of PREP-3: both indexes are built ONCE from the COMPLETE `entries` vector BEFORE `entries.truncate(cfg.corpus_cap)` (pass.rs:127-133) — the storage read `seed_corpus` (storage/src/seed_impl.rs:50) applies no LIMIT, so the pass receives the whole corpus and the cap is the only truncation; building over the capped vector would make a same-named parent beyond the cap invisible, so a duplicate could read unique or a unique parent could not contribute): step (1) reads a PER-FILE index (path, qualified_name) → the doc of the first entry in corpus order with a canonical type subtype and a non-empty doc, or none, whose KEY SET records every (path, qualified_name) of an entry of ANY subtype, forward declarations skipped — key present ⇒ decided in that file (not a per-run map over the run at :171-196, which would miss a class cut from its run by the cap); step (2) reads a CORPUS-WIDE map over the entries with a canonical type subtype, forward declarations skipped: qualified_name → (the first such entry's doc, count of such entries), consulted only when count == 1; the capped run loop only CONSULTS the two indexes, so the admitted/emitted/`corpus_omitted` counts are unchanged (review SD-F03: L10 states no same-file limitation and the spike's measured lookup was same-file-or-unique-in-corpus — the C++ header/impl split: leveldb `db/db_impl.h:29` `class DBImpl : public DB {` with `db/db_impl.cc:292` `Status DBImpl::Recover(VersionEdit* edit, bool* save_manifest) {`; `db/db_iter.h:15` `class DBImpl;` is a forward declaration the C++ extractor stores with the same qualified name and `forward_decl: true` (cpp-extractor `forward_decl_class_is_flagged_definition_is_not`), so counting it would make every forward-declared class ambiguous and defeat the case the fallback exists for — hence ignored; and a same-file entry of any kind blocks the fallback because in that file it IS the method's name-parent, so a same-named type elsewhere is not its enclosing type — the spike's `by_file_qn` rule; leveldb stores 0 doc comments, so the fallback contributes nothing there); → `enclosing_doc_sentence(doc)` → passed to `build_chunk_document` (:252-256) (leveldb has 0 documented symbols, so the cross-file branch changes nothing there — stated; on FRAKTAG the 152 METHOD chunks with a documented same-file name-parent all sit under a CLASS (133) or an INTERFACE (19), so the kind gate changes no measured row — it makes the L10 invariant hold by construction rather than by corpus accident); `has_doc` (:237) and `is_field` (:241-246) are untouched (`non_method_children_embed_without_the_enclosing_sentence`: a PROPERTY and a CONSTRUCTOR of a documented class keep today's document and document_hash); the document hash (:257) is the copy-forward reuse key (:150-161, :272-289), so every METHOD chunk whose enclosing type carries a doc gets a NEW `document_hash` and is re-embedded ONCE on the first pass after this change (`reused` = 0 for those; the model_change test's mechanism, now triggered by composition) — the stated cost of RG-REQ-010-L10, reported per corpus in the evidence; pass_tests.rs helper `doc_hash` (:13-15; its `build_chunk_document` call is :14) gains the argument (its callers pass `None`; the existing tests' `chunk` helper builds FUNCTION entries, so their documents are unchanged). Eleven NEW pass tests, the eleven names in the command (a fake corpus: `enclosing_type_sentence_enters_the_method_document_and_its_reuse_key`: a documented class `C` with a method `C.m` in file `a.ts` → `C.m`'s embedded text contains the class sentence and its `document_hash` differs from the no-enclosing composition; `same_file_type_parent_wins_over_a_cross_file_one`: a class `D` documented in `a.ts` AND another documented `D` in `b.ts`, with `D.m` in `a.ts` → `D.m` carries `a.ts`'s sentence; `unique_cross_file_type_parent_contributes_its_sentence`: a class `E` documented only in `e.h` with `E.m` (subtype METHOD) in `e.cc` → `E.m` carries `E`'s sentence and its `document_hash` differs from the no-enclosing composition; `ambiguous_cross_file_type_parents_contribute_no_sentence`: a class `F` documented in both `f1.h` and `f2.h` with `F.m` in `f.cc` → `F.m` embeds without a sentence, document and hash byte-identical to today's; `same_file_name_parent_blocks_the_cross_file_fallback`: in `h.ts` an UNDOCUMENTED class `H` with METHOD `H.m` and a documented VARIABLE `v` with METHOD `v.m`, and in `other.ts` a documented class `H` and a documented class `v` → `H.m` and `v.m` byte-identical to the no-enclosing composition (step (1) decides in the chunk's file; no other file's type is attributed); `forward_declaration_is_never_an_enclosing_type_candidate`: a documented class `G` defined in `g.h`, a forward declaration of `G` documented with a DIFFERENT sentence (CLASS, `forward_decl: SeedForwardDecl::ForwardDecl`) in `g_fwd.h`, and METHOD `G::m` in `g.cc` → `G::m` carries `g.h`'s sentence (the forward declaration neither supplies nor makes the name ambiguous — the leveldb `db_iter.h:15` shape); and a class `K` present only as a documented forward declaration in `k_fwd.h` with METHOD `K::m` in `k.cc` → `K::m` byte-identical to the no-enclosing composition; `unique_type_parent_beyond_the_corpus_cap_still_contributes_its_sentence`: `corpus_cap: 1`, a METHOD `Z::m` in `a.cc` (first in (path, line) order, so inside the cap) and a documented class `Z` only in `z.h` (beyond the cap) → `Z::m`'s document carries `z.h`'s sentence and its `document_hash` differs from the no-enclosing composition, while `report.admitted` = 1 and `report.corpus_omitted` = 1 (the class's own chunk is still not emitted); `second_type_parent_beyond_the_corpus_cap_makes_the_fallback_abstain`: `corpus_cap: 2`, a METHOD `Y::m` in `a.cc` and a documented class `Y` in `b.h` (both inside the cap) and a second documented class `Y` in `z.h` (beyond the cap) → `Y::m` byte-identical to the no-enclosing composition (the out-of-cap duplicate makes the name ambiguous), `report.admitted` = 2, `report.corpus_omitted` = 1; the existing `corpus_cap_omits_the_remainder` stays green unchanged (the cap still bounds the emitted vectors); `non_method_children_embed_without_the_enclosing_sentence`: a one-line undocumented PROPERTY `C.p` and a CONSTRUCTOR `C.constructor` of the documented class → documents and `document_hash` byte-identical to today's, `is_field` true for `C.p`; `documented_non_type_name_parent_gives_no_enclosing_sentence`: a documented FUNCTION `f` and a documented VARIABLE `v` in `a.ts` with METHOD chunks `f.m` and `v.m` in the same file → both documents and `document_hash` byte-identical to the no-enclosing composition (`doc_hash(qn, None, own doc, span)`), i.e. no sentence enters from a non-type; `each_canonical_type_subtype_encloses_a_method`: one documented parent per subtype CLASS, INTERFACE, STRUCT, ENUM, each with a METHOD child in the same file → each child's embedded text contains its parent's first sentence). rank.rs (13 tests), classify.rs/classify_tests.rs (31), ports.rs, hash.rs, storage seed_impl.rs, daemon-runtime seed/, rgr find/ are byte-identical (the diff --quiet): the floor `SEED_SIMILARITY_FLOOR = 0.30` (rgr seed_render.rs:51), the model `minishlab/potion-code-16M-v2` (daemon-runtime seed/local_engine.rs:49), the tiers and the partition are untouched

changeJustifications.summary: Adds the constant `MAX_ENCLOSING_SENTENCE_CHARS = 160` and two pure functions, `enclosing_doc_sentence` and `parent_qualified_name`. Adds a new second parameter `enclosing_sentence` to `build_chunk_document`; the output order is name, sentence, own doc, body, and `None` gives byte-identical output. Rewrites the false geometry paragraph and the module doc. Adds 6 tests; the existing callers gain `None`. Unchanged in revision 1.

Adds private `ENCLOSING_TYPE_SUBTYPES`, `METHOD_SUBTYPE` and `enclosing_sentences`. The latter applies the LOOKUP RULE over the complete pre-cap corpus: per-file key set first, then a unique corpus-wide canonical type. The results are truncated together with the entries and passed into `build_chunk_document`, so the sentence is part of document_hash. Revision 1 (SD-R-001): a single `takes_part` predicate (forward_decl != ForwardDecl) now gates both building the index and receiving a sentence. A C++ in-class method prototype therefore embeds exactly as before.

Updates the `doc_hash` helper to pass `None`. Adds fixture helpers and the 11 SD-C02-named tests. Revision 1 adds `forward_declared_method_receives_no_enclosing_sentence`: a documented class C in c.h, a forward-declared METHOD C::m in c.h, and the definition C::m in c.cc. The prototype's document and hash are byte-identical to the no-sentence form, while the definition receives the sentence.

OUTCOME, revision 1: SD-R-001 is fixed. All six checks were re-run on the revised candidate and passed (EXECUTED).

SD-R-001: I confirmed the reviewer's evidence. cpp-extractor `build_node_metadata` documents that `forward_decl` marks a type forward declaration or an in-class method prototype. Before the fix, `enclosing_sentences` excluded forward declarations only when building the parent indexes, so a prototype METHOD `C::m` in the class's header received the class sentence.

Defect class: a forward declaration took part in the enclosing-type lookup.

Rule that closes it: one predicate, `takes_part` (forward_decl != SeedForwardDecl::ForwardDecl), gates every role an entry can play. A forward declaration is never an index key, never supplies a sentence and never receives one. The `Unreadable` state is not a proven forward declaration and still takes part, as the LOOKUP RULE says ("genuine forward declarations"). The new fixture failed before the fix and passes after.
